explanation: Because children have lower physical reserves, a minor illness or breathing problem can quickly turn serious if we don't catch it early. You're building great clinical intuition!

question: Which chemical gets released when tissues get injured, causing local blood vessels to widen?

options.A: Amylase
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Histamine
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Histamine is the chemical alarm bell! When cells are damaged, histamine rushes out, widening blood vessels and letting fluids flood the area—giving us the classic signs of inflammation.

question: What is the recommended daily percentage range for total fat intake in healthy adults?
explanation: Aiming for 20% to 35% of daily calories from fats keeps adults energized and healthy without overdoing it. You're doing great!

question: Why do we restrict fat in certain diets rather than cutting it out completely?

options.A: Completely removing fat causes immediate weight gain.
options.B: The body still needs a minimal amount of fat for essential functions.
options.C: Fat-free foods are too expensive to produce.
options.D: Patients will refuse to eat any food without fat.

explanation: Even on a low-fat diet, our cells and organs need a little bit of fat to function properly and absorb vital nutrients!

question: Which strategy is most important when trying to shift a hospital's workplace culture?

options.A: Sending out a single memo explaining the new hospital mission statement
options.B: Threatening disciplinary action for anyone who questions hospital leadership
options.C: Implementing deliberate, sustained actions that embed new values into daily work
options.D: Replacing all senior nursing staff with new graduates from local universities

explanation: Spot on! Changing culture doesn't happen from a single memo; it takes consistent, long-term effort built into everyday ward routines.

question: What is the typical length of a normal menstrual cycle for an adult woman?

options.A: 40 to 50 days
options.B: 60 to 75 days
options.C: 21 to 35 days
options.D: 10 to 14 days

explanation: While textbooks love talking about a 28-day cycle, any cycle that consistently falls between 21 and 35 days is completely normal and healthy!

question: What is the main goal of managing an injured victim while they are inside a moving ambulance?

options.A: To complete all surgical procedures before hospital arrival
options.B: To prevent further injury and keep vital organs working
options.C: To diagnose the exact cause of the accident during transit
options.D: To discharge the patient home if vital signs stabilize

explanation: The transit phase focuses purely on stabilizing critical functions and protecting the patient from additional harm until they reach definitive care. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why is the hospital incident report kept separate from the patient's main medical chart?

options.A: It serves as the primary legal bill sent to the health insurance
options.B: It is used internally for quality improvement and risk management
options.C: It proves that no mistake ever happened during the shift
options.D: It allows the patient to edit the nursing notes at home

explanation: Incident reports are special internal tools. They help the hospital track safety trends and fix systems, rather than acting as patient records.

question: How do prospective study findings directly benefit frontline nurses working in clinical wards?

options.A: By providing historical background on ancient medical discoveries
options.B: By eliminating the need for patient assessments during night shifts
options.C: By replacing all bedside charting with automated computer algorithms
options.D: By helping identify high-risk patients early so preventative nursing care can be applied

explanation: Prospective research uncovers risk factors that frontline nurses use to spot vulnerable patients and prevent adverse hospital events. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h7)

question: What do we call it when a patient's pulse and breathing finally come back after cardiac arrest?

options.A: Reactive cardiac stabilization
options.B: Reversed ventricular failure
options.C: Return of spontaneous circulation
options.D: Resuscitated electrical rhythm

explanation: In hospital slang, we call this ROSC (Return of Spontaneous Circulation). It means the heart is beating on its own again with a feelable pulse!

question: What makes pathological waste different from normal trash?

options.A: Pathological waste is generated exclusively in hospital kitchens.
options.B: Pathological waste consists of recognizable human tissues and body parts.
options.C: Pathological waste includes only broken glass and empty medicine vials.
options.D: Pathological waste is composed strictly of administrative paper records.

explanation: Pathological waste refers to body tissues and parts. Because of what they are, they need special, respectful handling and high-heat burning.

question: Which breathing pattern features deep, fast breaths followed by a temporary pause in breathing?

options.A: Biot respiration
options.B: Apneustic breathing
options.C: Cheyne-Stokes respiration
options.D: Kussmaul breathing

explanation: Cheyne-Stokes breathing has regular cycles of breaths getting deeper and faster, then slowing down into a short pause (apnea). It's very common near the end of life.

question: What hormone stimulates the gallbladder to contract and release bile into the small intestine?

options.A: Secretin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Cholecystokinin (CCK)
options.D: Gastrin

explanation: CCK is released in response to dietary fats and proteins, causing the gallbladder to release stored bile. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h8)

question: Who is most likely to act as the primary day-to-day caregiver for a patient recovering at home?

options.A: Family members living with or near the client
options.B: The contracted medical equipment delivery driver
options.C: Voluntary auditors from the federal government
options.D: The regional health commissioner on duty

explanation: That's right! In our setting, family is everything. Loved ones usually do the heavy lifting of supporting patients between our visits.

question: Why is obstructed labor more common among very young mothers?

options.A: Cephalopelvic disproportion caused by an immature pelvis
options.B: Premature hardening of the fetal cranial bones
options.C: Excessive physical exercise during the third trimester
options.D: Over-consumption of dietary iron during the first trimester

explanation: Spot on! Because a young girl's pelvis is still growing, it might be too small for the baby's head to pass through easily.

question: Why does a failure in cell death (apoptosis) lead to autoimmune disease?

options.A: Bone marrow stops making new white blood cells
options.B: Pathogens are allowed to hide inside dying cells
options.C: Healthy cells die too quickly and release too many nutrients
options.D: Autoreactive lymphocytes survive instead of undergoing programmed cell death

explanation: Normally, rogue immune cells that could attack our body are told to self-destruct. When that fails, these harmful cells stick around and cause trouble.

question: Why must a nurse wash their hands immediately after removing gloves?

options.A: Gloves can have tiny invisible defects and hands can become contaminated during removal
options.B: Soap helps preserve the natural oils in the skin of the hands
options.C: Hospital policy requires handwashing only before putting on gloves
options.D: It removes any lingering powder left inside the glove material

explanation: Microscopic leaks or accidental contamination during glove stripping means hands are rarely completely clean underneath. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is the main goal of putting people in quarantine during an outbreak?

options.A: To cure chronic non-communicable diseases in regional health centers
options.B: To restrict movement of healthy people exposed to infection during the incubation period
options.C: To punish people who refuse to take their prescribed preventive medications
options.D: To provide specialized intensive care for patients with severe organ failure

explanation: Quarantine keeps exposed but healthy people away from others just to watch and see if symptoms show up.

question: How does low socioeconomic status typically impact a patient's long-term adaptation to a chronic illness?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for professional nursing care
options.B: It forces the body to stop experiencing the alarm stage of stress
options.C: It automatically guarantees a faster psychological recovery
options.D: It can limit access to essential medications and healthy nutrition

explanation: Financial hardship restricts access to necessary health resources, making sustained disease management and adaptation significantly harder. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h4)

question: A patient's pulse oximeter shows 82%, but they are talking and breathing easily. What should you do first?

options.A: Turn off the monitor because it is definitely broken
options.B: Immediately start chest compressions and call a code blue
options.C: Check the physical patient and look for cold fingers or nail polish
options.D: Assume the patient is in severe respiratory distress

explanation: Always assess your patient before the machine! Poor circulation or dark nail polish often causes false low readings. Great nursing instinct!

question: Roughly how many extra calories per day does producing breast milk require on average?

options.A: 100 calories
options.B: 1200 calories
options.C: 50 calories
options.D: 500 calories

explanation: Milk production is metabolically demanding, requiring about 500 extra calories daily for an exclusively breastfeeding mother. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h2)

question: About how long is a standard research abstract?

options.A: 50 words
options.B: 1000 words
options.C: 250 words
options.D: 500 words

explanation: An abstract is a quick, bite-sized summary—usually kept around 250 words so busy nurses can read it in a minute!

question: What is a common socioeconomic barrier to good nutrition?

options.A: Inability to afford fresh, nutrient-dense food items
options.B: Excessive availability of free drinking water
options.C: A lack of personal interest in human anatomy
options.D: Too many cooking utensils in the household kitchen

explanation: Poverty and low income restrict access to quality food, often forcing reliance on cheap, calorie-dense foods with low nutritional value. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h7)

question: How do researchers usually find common themes in qualitative interview notes?

options.A: By selecting only the longest interview and ignoring all the others
options.B: By throwing away any interview answer that does not match their personal opinion
options.C: By reading through the text repeatedly to identify patterns and grouping similar ideas
options.D: By feeding every sentence into a calculator to find the mathematical mean

explanation: Thematic analysis takes patience: researchers read the text over and over to spot patterns and group similar ideas together.

question: What is the main purpose of taking mental health care out into the community?

options.A: To replace all general hospitals with psychiatric units
options.B: To force patients into long-term institutional confinement
options.C: To eliminate the need for any trained medical personnel
options.D: To shift mental health care closer to people's living spaces and reduce stigma

explanation: Bringing care to the community makes it friendly, accessible, and helps chase away the fear and stigma attached to mental illness.

question: You just received a new supply of liquid pentavalent vaccines for your clinic fridge. Where should you place them?

options.A: Packed tightly inside the door racks in multiple layers
options.B: On the middle shelves, away from freezer walls
options.C: Inside a sealed container filled with unconditioned ice
options.D: Directly touching the floor of the freezer compartment

explanation: Pentavalent vaccines hate freezing! Keep them safely on the middle shelves where the temperature stays stable and above freezing.

question: As a fresh graduate, what is the very first official step you must take toward getting your license?

options.A: Payment of lifetime indemnity insurance fees to the federal treasury
options.B: Immediate appointment as a senior nursing officer in a teaching hospital
options.C: Submission of architectural drawings of a proposed private clinic
options.D: Educational verification of certificates from an accredited school

explanation: Before you write board exams or get your license, the council first needs to confirm that you actually graduated from an approved nursing school.

question: What is the primary purpose of a policy brief?

options.A: To display raw, unedited statistical calculations and formulas
options.B: To document the personal biography of the lead researcher
options.C: To provide concise, actionable recommendations for decision-makers
options.D: To serve as a textbook for first-year nursing students

explanation: Policy briefs summarize research for busy leaders so they can easily make informed decisions and rule changes. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which bacteria is famously spread through raw milk and causes undulant fever?

options.A: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.B: Lactobacillus acidophilus
options.C: Brucella species
options.D: Clostridium botulinum

question: Which assessment is essential when checking a newborn's skull after a difficult birth with heavy moulding?

options.A: Checking deep tendon reflexes in the lower extremities only

options.C: Measuring head circumference and assessing fontanelle texture

question: What is a core day-to-day duty of nurses and midwives in Nigerian reproductive health care?

options.A: Providing direct clinical care, health education, and community outreach
options.B: Writing national health insurance laws in the federal legislature
options.C: Manufacturing contraceptive implants in national laboratories
options.D: Importing specialized surgical instruments from overseas

explanation: Exactly! Nurses and midwives are on the frontline, delivering care at the bedside and educating communities on healthy living.

question: What is a common emotional response experienced by a person who has recently acquired a permanent physical disability?

options.A: Complete indifference toward their physical health status
options.B: Immediate and permanent acceptance of the new lifestyle
options.C: Euphoria over lifestyle changes and reduced responsibilities
options.D: Grief and a process similar to mourning a loss

explanation: Patients frequently experience a grief reaction as they process the loss of their previous physical abilities and independence. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h6)

question: What is the main goal of doing a statistical test on a research hypothesis?

options.A: To calculate the exact number of patients needed for a trial
options.B: To prove the null hypothesis is always correct
options.C: To see if there is enough evidence to reject the null hypothesis
options.D: To replace the alternative hypothesis with a descriptive chart

explanation: Spot on! We test our data to see if we have enough strong proof to throw out the null hypothesis and say our intervention actually works.

question: Why do so many teenagers today end up low on vitamin D?

options.A: Consuming too many citrus fruits and juices
options.B: Drinking excessive amounts of plain water
options.C: Avoiding all forms of dietary protein
options.D: Spending less time outdoors in natural sunlight

explanation: You nailed it! Our bodies make vitamin D from sunlight on the skin. With more indoor time and screen sessions, teens get less natural sun exposure.

question: What is the main legal fear many healthcare workers have about apologizing?

options.A: That hospital management will cut their monthly housing allowances
options.B: That the nursing council will revoke their license within twenty-four hours
options.C: That patients will demand free medication for the rest of their lives
options.D: That saying sorry will be used as an immediate admission of legal liability

explanation: Many nurses worry that saying 'I'm sorry' will be used in court as a direct confession that they were negligent.

question: Why does the center of a developing cartilage model start to calcify?

options.A: Chondrocytes hypertrophy and restrict nutrient diffusion through the matrix
options.B: Synovial fluid leaks into the center of the shaft
options.C: Local nerve endings stimulate mineral crystallization
options.D: Osteoclasts deposit excess calcium directly into the cartilage

explanation: As the cartilage cells (chondrocytes) in the middle grow large, they block nutrients from passing through, causing the center to harden and change.

question: Why do modern clinical guidelines prefer Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) over traditional sharp metal curettage?

options.A: MVA is associated with less pain, lower complication rates, and quicker recovery
options.B: Sharp curettage instruments are too expensive for most developing nations
options.C: MVA completely eliminates the need for any pre-procedure pain medication
options.D: Sharp curettage requires general anesthesia in an operating theatre every time

explanation: You nailed it! MVA is gentler on the uterine lining and poses lower risks of perforation compared to sharp metal curettage.

question: When someone pushes back against your advocacy campaign, which of these should you NOT do?

options.A: Dismissing the critic's concerns as foolish and uneducated
options.B: Anticipating counter-arguments ahead of time with solid data
options.C: Acknowledging their point of view respectfully before pivoting
options.D: Remaining calm, professional, and prepared with evidence

explanation: Never insult or dismiss your critics! Staying respectful keeps your credibility high, even when people disagree with you.

question: Why do some rectally administered drugs avoid the liver's first-pass metabolism?

options.A: The rectal wall completely destroys all liver enzymes
options.B: Lymph nodes absorb the entire dose before it reaches blood vessels
options.C: Lower rectal veins drain directly into systemic circulation
options.D: Medications bypass the bloodstream and enter the kidneys

explanation: Blood from the inferior rectal veins goes straight to the inferior vena cava, bypassing the liver on its first trip around the body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h2)

question: A clinic treats every patient with the same high standard of care, whether they are rich, poor, or from any tribe. What quality dimension is this?

options.A: Timeliness
options.B: Effectiveness
options.C: Efficiency
options.D: Equity

explanation: Spot on! Equity means fairness. No patient's background or pocket should ever determine the quality of care they receive from you. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is the biggest advantage of giving a client card directly to the patient to keep?

options.A: It saves the clinic money on buying storage cabinets
options.B: It prevents the clinic from ever writing anything down
options.C: It forces the patient to become a trained community health worker
options.D: The patient carries their health history with them to any new facility

explanation: Exactly right! Portable client cards ensure a patient's immunization and health history travels with them safely, even if they move away.

question: What is the nurse's main role when a patient wants to use alternative therapies?

options.A: Forbidding the use of any treatment not taught in medical school
options.B: Ignoring the patient's personal beliefs to focus only on drugs
options.C: Coordinating care safely while respecting patient preferences
options.D: Personally performing every alternative therapy session

explanation: Nurses bridge the gap! We respect what matters to the patient while making sure their overall treatment plan stays safe and effective.

question: Where does the fluid from the lymph vessels in the external genitalia primarily drain?

options.A: Deep pelvic lymph nodes only

options.C: Axillary lymph nodes in the chest
options.D: Superficial inguinal lymph nodes

question: A nurse reads a study and wonders if the results can safely apply to patients in her own local hospital. Which concept is she checking?

options.A: External validity
options.B: Intervention bias
options.C: Instrument reliability
options.D: Internal consistency

explanation: External validity is all about the real world. It asks: can we take these study results and successfully apply them to other patients outside the original study setting?

question: Why is the bedside nurse considered the central link in the healthcare nutrition team?

options.A: They have legal power to prescribe diets
options.B: They do all formal nutrition assessments alone
options.C: They observe daily intake and update the team
options.D: They are the only ones allowed to serve food

question: Which antiseptic needs to dry on the skin so it can slowly release free iodine to kill germs?

options.A: Hexachlorophene
options.B: Chlorhexidine gluconate
options.C: Povidone-iodine
options.D: Isopropyl alcohol

explanation: Povidone-iodine needs a little drying time to work its magic and release free iodine onto your skin.

question: During a follow-up assessment, what must a nurse always screen for directly?

options.A: Thoughts of self-harm or harming others
options.B: The patient's favorite childhood memories
options.C: Recent changes in political opinions
options.D: The exact brand of soap the patient uses

explanation: Safety assessment, including checking for suicidal or aggressive thoughts, is a mandatory part of every mental health evaluation. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h4)

question: Right after the placenta is safely delivered, what is your next immediate nursing action?

options.A: Massage the uterine fundus to ensure it remains firm and contracted
options.B: Transfer the mother immediately to the operating theatre for suturing
options.C: Check the newborn's vital signs and complete the Apgar scoring chart
options.D: Administer a second dose of IV fluids containing magnesium sulfate

explanation: Give that fundus a gentle massage! It wakes up the muscle fibers so they squeeze shut on open blood vessels, stopping postpartum hemorrhage in its tracks.

question: Why do different agencies need to work together during a disaster response?

options.A: It gives nurses the authority to write new national laws
options.B: It replaces the need for community education and local drills
options.C: It guarantees that natural hazards will completely miss the country
options.D: It ensures that different groups do not duplicate efforts and waste resources

explanation: Brilliant! Sharing information and working hand-in-hand prevents confusion and keeps help running smoothly.

question: Why do teenagers often take sudden risks even when they know the dangers?

options.A: They deliberately ignore all forms of social interaction
options.B: Their hormone levels remain completely stable throughout the teenage years
options.C: They possess completely adult-like cognitive maturity in all situations
options.D: Their neurological risk assessment and impulse control circuits are still maturing

explanation: Exactly! Because the brain's risk-evaluating circuits are still growing, teens are more prone to acting on impulse without fully weighing the long-term consequences.

question: Why do local rescue teams worry so much about crowd control at a disaster site?

options.A: Crowds prevent media houses from broadcasting live updates
options.B: Uncontrolled crowds often steal heavy rescue machinery
options.C: Large crowds block access roads, delay ambulances, and endanger more lives
options.D: Onlookers are required by law to assist professional paramedics

explanation: You got it! Too many curious onlookers block the roads, stopping ambulances from getting through and putting even more people in danger.

question: Which of these is a true feature of a polysynaptic reflex arc?

options.A: Total absence of a sensory neuron component
options.B: Presence of one or more interneurons
options.C: Involvement of only a single chemical synapse
options.D: Speed that is always faster than monosynaptic reflexes

question: What does the term 'adverse selection' mean in community health insurance?

options.A: Doctors refuse to treat patients with insurance cards
options.B: Hospitals run out of essential drugs during emergencies
options.C: Only sick people join while healthy people stay out
options.D: The government cancels the health scheme suddenly

explanation: Adverse selection is a tricky challenge. When mostly sick people join and healthy people skip it, the insurance pool runs out of money because payouts are way higher than collected funds.

question: Why do researchers clean their data before running statistics?

options.A: To reduce the number of participants needed for the study
options.B: To catch entry mistakes and prevent false research results
options.C: To get extra funding from the hospital research committee
options.D: To make the research report shorter and easier to print

explanation: Data cleaning is like double-checking your medication dosage math—it catches errors early so your final results are accurate and safe.

question: Why do we bother grouping research studies into different types?

options.A: To make every clinical trial take less time to finish
options.B: To make reading journals and finding study types easier
options.C: To ensure that all patients receive the exact same treatment
options.D: To increase the financial funding for the hospital

explanation: You've got this! Grouping research designs simply helps nurses quickly understand how a study was done and what kind of evidence it brings to the table. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h1)

question: How do rumors and misinformation about vaccine safety affect community coverage?

options.A: They increase caregiver hesitancy and lead to missed vaccinations
options.B: They force health workers to improve the cold chain system
options.C: They have no real impact on routine immunization numbers
options.D: They make parents bring their children to the clinic much earlier

explanation: When parents hear false safety claims, fear stops them from allowing their children to receive life-saving vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h2)

question: What is the single most important action to stop contact infections from spreading in a hospital?

options.A: Administering prophylactic antibiotics to all new admissions
options.B: Wearing sterile surgical masks during visiting hours
options.C: Proper hand hygiene before and after patient contact
options.D: Changing bed linens twice daily for every patient

explanation: Never underestimate simple handwashing! It is your absolute best defense against carrying germs between patients.

question: What is the primary goal of rational drug use?

options.A: Making sure patients take every single pill prescribed without missing a dose
options.B: Eliminating the need for doctors to write paper prescriptions in the ward
options.C: Ensuring patients receive the right medication and dose for their clinical needs
options.D: Reducing the overall hospital budget spent on purchasing expensive antibiotics

explanation: Rational drug use focuses primarily on meeting the specific clinical needs of the patient with the correct drug and dose. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why might some families try to hide harmful traditional practices from community health nurses during home visits?

options.A: Cultural laws that forbid speaking to healthcare workers in private
options.B: Ignorance regarding the exact location of the nearest health center
options.C: Belief that nurses are legally required to provide free food supplies
options.D: Fear of legal penalties or social judgment from health authorities

explanation: Because practices like child marriage or FGM are increasingly against the law, families hide them out of fear. Building trust as a nurse is the best way to gently break through this wall.

question: What is a major downside of simply criminalizing FGM without first educating the community?

options.A: All rural families suddenly move to the cities
options.B: Traditional cutters happily hand their tools over to the police
options.C: Healthcare workers completely take over the practice
options.D: The practice goes underground and becomes much harder to track

explanation: Spot on! When laws are introduced without winning community hearts and minds, practitioners just do the cuts in secret, which actually increases health risks.

question: Why is a home care nurse in a great position to notice a client's emotional and mental state?

options.A: They enter private spaces where clients feel comfortable letting their guard down
options.B: They focus exclusively on mental health rather than physical care
options.C: They have advanced psychiatric training required by law
options.D: They spend less time with clients than hospital nurses do

explanation: Visiting someone in their own home lets you see the real picture. Clients are often more relaxed and open in their personal space than they'd ever be in a busy clinic ward.

question: What happens when communication breaks down during a disaster response?

options.A: The federal government automatically increases funding for local clinics
options.B: International aid organizations decide to withdraw completely from the region
options.C: Rescue efforts stall and resources are wasted due to lack of coordination
options.D: Community members become more resilient against future emergencies

explanation: Good communication is everything! Without it, teams duplicate work or miss sending help to where it's needed most.

question: What is the defining feature of a Cost-Benefit Analysis in healthcare?

options.A: Outcomes are measured strictly in natural clinical units like blood pressure
options.B: Both costs and health outcomes are measured in monetary terms
options.C: It completely ignores financial expenses to focus on patient emotions
options.D: It is only used when two treatments produce identical results

explanation: In a Cost-Benefit Analysis, even the health outcomes are converted into money (like naira). This lets you directly compare cash spent to cash saved or earned.

question: A head nurse gives a junior nurse more independence after watching her successfully master wound dressings. What leadership style is this?

options.A: Transactional leadership
options.B: Situational leadership
options.C: Trait leadership theory
options.D: Laissez-faire leadership

explanation: Well done! Situational leaders adapt their approach to fit the changing skill level and confidence of their team members.

question: What do we mean by "abnormal illness behaviour"?

options.A: Seeking help immediately after experiencing severe trauma
options.B: A response that is out of proportion to actual physical findings
options.C: Following all medical advice given by the attending nurse
options.D: Recovering from a minor illness within expected timeframes

explanation: This happens when the reaction doesn't match the medical reality—like complete denial of a serious condition, or intense panic over a tiny scratch.

question: What is one major win of using electronic health records instead of digging through heavy paper files?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for nurses to write narrative notes
options.B: Information is instantly accessible across multiple hospital departments
options.C: It prevents patients from ever viewing their own medical history
options.D: Computers make clinical judgment and assessment completely automatic

explanation: Exactly! Digital records mean no more running physical folders across the hospital. Authorized staff in different units can view charts at the same time, making teamwork so much smoother.

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for managing hereditary conditions?

options.A: It removes the need for nurses to speak directly with patients
options.B: Hospital regulations require at least ten staff members for every patient
options.C: No single profession has all the skills needed to address complex genetic and social needs
options.D: It ensures that laboratory scientists make all final clinical decisions

explanation: Hereditary conditions involve medical, emotional, and social challenges that require diverse expertise from multiple healthcare professionals. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h7)

question: Why does a patient continue to experience monthly menstrual periods after getting her tubes tied?

options.A: The ovaries and uterus remain completely functional.
options.B: The uterine lining regenerates independently of the tubes.
options.C: Fallopian tubes still produce blood flow monthly.
options.D: Synthetic hormones are provided through daily medications.

explanation: The procedure only blocks the path of the egg and sperm; it does not touch the ovaries or the uterus, so hormone production and regular menstruation continue as normal. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h1)

question: What is the proper technique for cleaning a patient's skin before giving an injection?

options.A: Use a circular motion starting from the center and moving outward.
options.B: Clean from the outer edges inward toward the exact puncture spot.
options.C: Wipe back and forth rapidly across the site with a dry gauze pad.
options.D: Apply warm soapy water and rinse with sterile tap water.

explanation: Well done! Starting from the center and swirling outwards pushes germs away from the exact spot where the needle will pierce the skin.

question: Besides normal vital signs, what else must a nurse check during a rehab assessment?

options.A: Functional ability and home environment safety
options.B: National health insurance policy rates
options.C: Pharmaceutical manufacturing costs
options.D: Hospital administrative budgeting records

explanation: A good rehab assessment looks at how well the patient can move around and whether their home is safe for them to return to.

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in clinical practice?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing disposable syringes
options.B: To speed up medication administration during busy ward shifts
options.C: To ensure patients experience zero pain during every procedure
options.D: To prevent harm to patients, healthcare workers, and the community

explanation: Injection safety encompasses protective measures for everyone involved in or affected by the injection process, preventing infections and injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why do many patients stop taking their blood pressure medication without telling their nurse?

options.A: They feel fine and assume the condition has gone away.
options.B: The medications always cure hypertension within one week.
options.C: Blood pressure pills taste sweet like candy.
options.D: Doctors prefer patients to stop taking pills after a month.

explanation: Because high blood pressure is asymptomatic, patients often mistake feeling well for being cured and abandon their regimen. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h5)

question: Why do nurse researchers often choose quasi-experimental designs instead of true experiments in actual clinical settings?

options.A: Hospital management refuses to let nurses use numerical data collection tools
options.B: True experiments are entirely illegal in clinical nursing environments
options.C: Quasi-experimental studies require no ethical approval or patient consent
options.D: It is often impossible to randomly assign patients to groups in a real hospital setting

explanation: In real-world wards, we work with existing groups of patients and staff, making strict random assignment tricky or impossible.

question: When should an intraosseous (IO) line be considered during resuscitation?

options.A: As the absolute first choice before trying any peripheral IV line
options.B: When the patient refuses to receive medications through the arm
options.C: Only after the patient achieves a return of spontaneous circulation
options.D: When intravenous access is difficult or taking too long to establish

explanation: IO access goes straight into the bone marrow and works as fast as an IV when placing a peripheral line fails. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why must a stroke client pass a swallow test before you give them normal food?

options.A: To check if the client has an allergy to hospital cutlery
options.B: To prevent food from entering the airway and causing aspiration pneumonia
options.C: To ensure the stomach can digest heavy proteins and fats
options.D: To find out which specific food flavors the client prefers to eat

explanation: Stroke weakness can make throat muscles sluggish, meaning food or water can easily slip down the 'wrong pipe' into the lungs instead of the belly.

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended strategy for preventing harm from gishiri cuts?

options.A: Providing emergency obstetric services
options.B: Expanding access to skilled antenatal care
options.C: Community health education on pelvic anatomy
options.D: Training traditional birth attendants to perform safer cuts

explanation: The goal is to stop the practice entirely rather than make cutting safer, as the procedure itself lacks any medical validity. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h7)

question: Which of these shows direct clinical competence during a nurse's evaluation?

options.A: The total number of personal phone calls made on duty
options.B: How well the nurse gets along with the hospital director
options.C: Correct medication administration technique
options.D: Whether the nurse wears fashionable shoes to work

explanation: Clinical competence is all about the actual nursing care you give. Getting your drug calculations and administration spot-on is a classic example!

question: Which principle ensures that vulnerable and quiet voices are heard during community health projects?

options.A: Equity
options.B: Profit
options.C: Isolation
options.D: Speed

explanation: Equity makes sure that everyone, especially the poor and marginalized, gets a fair chance to participate and benefit. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why are nursing audits so important for quality assurance?

options.A: They reduce the cost of purchasing hospital medications
options.B: They help discover gaps between standard care and actual practice
options.C: They guarantee that patients will never experience complications
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for physician supervision

explanation: Spot on! By comparing what we actually do against established guidelines, audits show us clearly where our care needs a little extra boost.

question: Which communication channel works best for reaching people in remote rural areas in their own language?

options.A: Radio broadcasts
options.B: Academic journals
options.C: Official letters
options.D: Social media posts

explanation: Radio is a powerful tool in Nigeria, reaching deep into rural communities where smartphones and internet might not be available.

question: What term is used when a reflex response is completely missing?

options.A: Autonomic dysreflexia
options.B: Neuromuscular fatigue
options.C: Hyperreflexia
options.D: Areflexia

explanation: Areflexia means the reflex is absent ('a-' meaning without). If it's just very weak, we call it hyporeflexia. You've got this!

question: Why are pregnant women and young children grouped together as a special population?

options.A: They take up most of the housing budget
options.B: They do not pay any community taxes by law
options.C: They share unique health vulnerabilities and face high risks of preventable illness
options.D: They are required to stay in the hospital continuously

explanation: Spot on! Mothers and young kids go through sensitive stages of life where quick, targeted health support can prevent major illnesses. They're a top priority in community nursing!

question: Why are finger foods often recommended for patients in the middle to late stages of dementia?

options.A: They make eating easier for patients who struggle with utensils
options.B: They eliminate the need for any supervision during meal times
options.C: They guarantee the patient will consume more protein than meat stews
options.D: They prevent the patient from ever dropping crumbs on the floor

explanation: Using forks and spoons can become too complex. Finger foods help patients feed themselves independently and keep up their nutrition.

question: Which public health measure helps protect people from getting human papillomavirus (HPV)?

options.A: Surgical removal
options.B: Daily antibiotics
options.C: Vaccination
options.D: Vitamin C therapy

explanation: You got it! Vaccines are our best primary defense because they train the immune system to fight off viruses like HPV before exposure ever happens.

question: Which antibody is the main culprit behind fast allergic drug reactions?

options.A: IgA
options.B: IgG
options.C: IgM
options.D: IgE

explanation: Immunoglobulin E (IgE) is the allergy antibody. It sticks to mast cells and sets off a quick release of histamine.

question: As a nurse, what is your main role right before giving a medicine to a patient?

options.A: Approving new drug formulas for clinical trials
options.B: Acting as the final safety check against medication errors
options.C: Prescribing appropriate dosages for admitted patients
options.D: Manufacturing safe pharmaceutical drugs for the hospital

explanation: You are the last line of defense! By checking the order, the drug, and the patient one last time, you make sure no mistakes reach them. You've got this!

question: What stops your windpipe (trachea) from squishing or collapsing when you breathe?

options.A: Surfactant produced by the lining
options.B: C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage
options.C: Positive pressure from the chest
options.D: Thick layers of skeletal muscle

explanation: Exactly! Those sturdy C-shaped cartilage rings keep your airway open wide and clear at all times.

question: Which of these is a direct cause of maternal morbidity?

options.A: Pregnancy-induced diabetes
options.B: Chronic malaria infection
options.C: Severe sickle cell anemia
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Direct causes come straight from the obstetric process itself—like heavy bleeding (hemorrhage) right after childbirth. You'll see this often on the ward!

question: What does Gross National Product (GNP) measure?

options.A: The total value of goods and services produced by a country's citizens
options.B: The total cost of running public hospitals across the country
options.C: The total expenditure on imported drugs and medical equipment
options.D: The total amount of money borrowed by the federal government annually

explanation: Think of GNP as the big picture: it adds up the total value of everything produced by a nation's citizens and businesses, no matter where in the world they are working. You've got this!

question: What does process data measure in a quality improvement project?

options.A: Patient satisfaction ratings collected after outpatient visits
options.B: The final health status of a patient after discharge
options.C: The total financial budget allocated to a specific ward
options.D: How healthcare services and nursing tasks are delivered

explanation: Process data is all about the *actions* we take. It checks if our day-to-day nursing tasks and clinical steps are actually being done.

question: Why is regular kit auditing and replenishment essential for community health programs?

options.A: To keep the outer packaging looking clean and professional
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing bulk supplies
options.C: To comply with paperwork demands from hospital administrators
options.D: To ensure supplies are not expired when an emergency birth occurs

explanation: Emergency kits are useless if items have degraded, expired, or been removed, making routine stock checks vital for community readiness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h7)

question: What is the main goal of actively managing the third stage of labour?

options.A: To eliminate the need to clean the perineum
options.B: To help breast milk come in much faster
options.C: To reduce the chances of primary postpartum haemorrhage
options.D: To prevent breathing difficulties in the newborn

explanation: Active management combines smart steps—like giving a uterotonic and controlled cord traction—to deliver the placenta smoothly and keep blood loss to a minimum.

question: A patient with a history of heart attacks is discharged without being given a statin or beta-blocker. What is this patient at higher risk for?

options.A: Immediate kidney failure caused by excessive medication
options.B: Acute drug toxicity from an accidental double dose
options.C: Severe antibiotic resistance from prolonged drug exposure
options.D: A recurrent cardiac event due to lack of secondary prevention

explanation: Brilliant! Leaving out essential recovery drugs (secondary prevention) significantly increases the chance that the patient might suffer another heart attack or stroke.

question: As student nurses, why do we bother learning and doing nursing research?

options.A: To build an evidence base for safe patient care
options.B: To replace traditional bedside nursing duties entirely
options.C: To prove that old hospital policies are useless
options.D: To complicate simple clinical procedures

explanation: You got this! Research gives us solid proof and reliable facts so we can take care of our patients safely and with confidence.
